rows: What is the most agriculturally productive soil order?
Mollisols — thick dark mollic epipedon; high SOM; high base saturation; temperate grasslands
E horizon (bleached, clay-depleted) + Bhs (dark Fe/Al/OM accumulation)
What diagnostic horizon is required for an Alfisol?
Why are Oxisols low in CEC despite being clay-rich?
Dominated by kaolinite (1:1 low CEC) and Fe/Al oxides (near-zero CEC); all 2:1 high-CEC clays weathered away
What does a Bg horizon indicate?
Gleying — periodic or permanent saturation with reducing conditions; hydric soil; gray from Fe reduction
Toposequence — series of soils varying systematically with topographic position under same climate and parent material
